summary: Childan navigates the social protocols of San Francisco, securing an incredibly rare mint copy of Volume One, Number One of Tip Top Comics from the 1930s as his gift for Tagomi's mysterious client. His internal reflections on German achievements (space flights, African colonization) and his resentment of American subordination to Japan reveal his contradictory values: he acknowledges German brutality yet admires their ambition and efficiency. Approaching the Nippon Times Building, Childan employs a black porter to carry his bags, maintaining the social distance required to avoid losing 'place.' He ascends to Tagomi's twentieth-floor office in an express elevator filled mostly with Japanese businessmen. Meanwhile, Juliana Frink is introduced living in Canon City, Colorado, working as a judo instructor. She watches Nazi rocket ships pass overhead and contemplates suicide while flirting with a young Italian truck driver named Joe, who is bitterly aware of his marginalized status in American society under Nazi influence. At the San Francisco airport, Mr. Baynes descends from a Lufthansa rocket and encounters an aggressive young Nazi artist, Alex Lotze, who makes prejudiced comments about Japanese architecture. Baynes reveals to Lotze (and to himself through this confession) that he is secretly a Jew who has undergone plastic surgery to pass as Aryan, part of a hidden network of Jews living unseen in Nazi society. He threatens to report Lotze to Nazi authorities. Meeting Tagomi at the airport, Baynes is immediately gifted with Childan's valuable Tip Top Comics find.

themes.name: The value of artifacts and culture

philosophical_concepts.name: The power of artifacts to preserve meaning

key_events: Childan finds the rare Tip Top Comics
Juliana's encounter with Joe at the diner
Baynes reveals his Jewish identity to Lotze
Tagomi presents the gift to Baynes
Baynes meets Tagomi and agrees to go to hotel
narrative_observations: PKD expands the world through multiple POV characters, revealing different aspects of the alternate history. Juliana's storyline introduces personal agency and moral choice outside the San Francisco power structure. Baynes' revelation is pivotal—he represents hidden resistance and the psychological toll of living under totalitarian surveillance. The prose shifts to reflect each character's internal preoccupations.
